Facsimile

fak-SIM-uh-lee -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, SIM; the ending is 'lee,' not 'mile.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Facsimile is an exact copy, especially of a document or printed material.

The historical society sells a facsimile of the town's 1850 newspaper, complete with its original advertisements.

Worked Example

A film studio needs a famous painting for a heist movie, but the real one never leaves its gallery. So a specialist spends four months producing a copy -- matching every brushstroke, every hairline crack in the varnish -- until even the gallery's own curator has to lean in close to tell the two apart.

The painter has produced a facsimile: an exact copy, faithful to the original in every detail. A facsimile is honest about what it is -- unlike a forgery, it never pretends to BE the original; its whole job is to match the original so the real thing can stay safe.

How Facsimile Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

replica

replica: an exact copy or model of something

duplicate

duplicate: an identical copy

reproduction

reproduction: a copy made of an original work

Antonyms

original

original: the real, first thing itself

genuine article

genuine article: the authentic item, not a copy

How Strong Is It? — duplicate → facsimile → replica

duplicate vs. facsimile

duplicate vs. facsimile: Duplicate says only that a second, identical copy exists -- a duplicate key, a duplicate file -- with no promise of craftsmanship.

replica vs. facsimile

replica vs. facsimile: Replica is the strongest of the three: a duplicate merely matches, but a replica has been painstakingly built to mirror the original in every visible detail, which is exactly the standard a facsimile is held to.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of facsimile.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — fac-

root — fac-: make, do (Latin facere 'to make')

root — simile

root — simile: like, similar (Latin similis 'like')

Put it together

Put it together: Facsimile is two Latin words fused together: fac simile, 'make it similar!' -- literally a command to a copyist. The word IS its own instruction: a facsimile is the result of someone making a thing as similar to the original as human hands allow. The office fax machine took its name from this word -- a fax is a facsimile sent down a phone line.

Use the root in a new word: manufacture

Use the root in a new word: manufacture: The plant can manufacture two thousand bicycles a week.

Root Check

Word Choice

Facsimile lives among documents and artifacts: a facsimile of a manuscript, a map, a signature, a first edition. It promises EXACTNESS -- 'a reasonable facsimile' is the joking way to admit a copy falls short. It is also the word hiding inside 'fax': a faxed page is literally a facsimile. A facsimile openly declares itself a copy; the moment a copy is passed off as the original, the right word becomes forgery.
